profile.name: Toni Guillem
profile.title: Technical Game Designer
profile.intro: I design the way games play. Then I get in the engine and make it happen.
profile.bio: My work sits between game design and implementation. I build gameplay abilities, shape combat systems, and turn design intentions into something a team can test and a player can feel.

projects.title: Rainbow Six Siege
projects.imageAlt: The Rainbow Six Siege operator roster
projects.label: Operator design / Systems / Balance
projects.summary: Small changes. Whole new ways to play.
projects.intro: Designing gadgets, reworking Operators, and balancing an interconnected tactical sandbox. My work on Siege covered new gameplay mechanics, player-facing systems, and the careful adjustment of a live competitive game.

sections.title: Lion: keeping the identity, changing the information
sections.body: Lion’s original global detection revealed enemy silhouettes and created problems at high levels of play. Our objective was to bring him back into the competitive Operator rotation. We moved his ability onto Siege’s existing Ping System while keeping an accessible, global ability. After monitoring the changes, Lion returned to Pro League in June 2019.

sections.title: Tachanka: a more mobile area-denial role
sections.body: The stationary turret limited Tachanka’s usefulness, but his identity mattered. I designed and prototyped a rework around an incendiary grenade launcher, testing the size and duration of its fire zones. We also converted his original LMG into a primary weapon, retaining its low rate of fire. I left Ubisoft after the design and full prototype were approved for production; the rework shipped in 2020.

sections.title: Gadgets with readable strengths and weaknesses
sections.body: The Proximity Alarm offered Defenders a small, throwable source of audio information. Its placement possibilities created combinations with other gadgets, while its vulnerability to EMP effects, explosions, gunfire, and melee provided counterplay. This feature shipped after my time at Ubisoft.

sections.title: The Bulletproof Camera
sections.body: I owned the design from a workshop concept through development with the Montréal team. The camera could see through smoke and resist frontal gunfire, with weak spots and other vulnerabilities creating counterplay. Its interactions with observation, EMP, smoke, and destruction systems were central to the design.

sections.title: Beyond individual Operators
sections.body: I worked with Data Analytics and User Research to evaluate balance changes, gathered feedback through professional-player workshops, and iterated through the Test Server. Earlier contributions included the concussion effect used by Ela and Zofia, Tactical Realism’s magazine management, team loadout information, weapon previews, and map concept proposals.

projects.title: United 1944
projects.imageAlt: United 1944 soldiers against orange battlefield artwork
projects.label: Shooter feel / Weapons / Design leadership
projects.summary: Building the foundations of a shooter.
projects.intro: A 16v16 multiplayer FPS combining combat with crafting, building, and tactical play. I led core gameplay design, turning the initial proof of concept into a more complete shooter experience in Unreal Engine 5.

sections.title: The feel of every shot
sections.body: I designed the core shooter system from scratch, including recoil, spread, and reload mechanics. This formed the foundation for more than 20 WWII weapons across over eight weapon families, supporting distinct combat roles and playstyles.

sections.title: A wider tactical toolkit
sections.body: Alongside the weapons, I conceptualized gadgets and passive abilities ranging from explosives to intelligence tools. The goal was to give players more ways to read an encounter and respond to it.

sections.title: Keeping the team aligned
sections.body: I worked with programming, animation, audio, and production to align gameplay with the creative direction. I also mentored a small team of designers, reviewing their work and helping them carry ideas from concept into the game.

projects.title: Assassin’s Creed Chronicles
projects.label: Level design / Quest design / UE3
projects.intro: Short, replayable missions set inside the Animus. I designed Challenge Room missions and built their layouts in Unreal Engine 3, working with Climax Studios in my first external co-development project at Ubisoft.

sections.title: A new rhythm for existing mechanics
sections.body: The brief was to create quickly accessible content alongside the main campaign. We developed three Challenge Room types: Collect, Contract, and Assassination. I combined the existing navigation, stealth, combat, and assassination mechanics into short missions with replay potential.

sections.title: The Animus as a design space
sections.body: I took levels from initial layout into Unreal Engine 3. The Animus’s abstract environment let us explore 2.5D navigation more freely than the main campaign’s realistic settings.

projects.title: Madden NFL 21 & PGA Tour
projects.label: Presentation / Progression / Team building
projects.intro: I joined EA SPORTS in January 2020 as the first game designer in a new Madrid division of EA Tiburon, helping translate the Orlando creative team’s vision into development work.

sections.title: Across teams and projects
sections.body: For the Stadia version of Madden NFL 21, I was the main game designer responsible for carrying through the franchise leadership’s creative vision. I then worked on presentation and player-progression features for PGA Tour. Alongside the Studio Director, I helped build the Madrid creative team, recruiting two designers.

projects.title: Hazel Dazzle
projects.imageAlt: Spherical planetary gameplay from Hazel Dazzle
projects.label: Gameplay programming / 3D puzzles
projects.summary: Where my design and programming met.
projects.intro: Two years leading game programming on an iPad adventure, with a small team and room to contribute directly to its design.

sections.title: Two kinds of space
sections.body: I engineered gameplay that moved between spherical 3D planetary navigation and isometric 2D dungeon exploration. My work included combo-based combat, character abilities, and an AI companion.

sections.title: A puzzle in your hands
sections.body: I designed a 3D puzzle system using the iPad’s accelerometer and gyroscope. Forced perspective helped make the screen feel like a physical box that players could manipulate in their hands.

projects.title: Burning Thirst
projects.label: Combat / Cinematics / Audio
projects.summary: The project that started it all.
projects.intro: A hack-and-slash game built by five students: three programmers and two artists. It was an early, ambitious project that helped me enter the games industry.

sections.title: Learning through a complete game
sections.body: I designed combat combos, fatalities, and special attacks, drawing on God of War 3 as a reference. I also designed, scripted, and implemented our cinematic system alongside an artist, with a narrative influenced by Grindhouse and Planet Terror, and took care of the game’s audio design.
